new_beads.why: Split from BD-067 (audit note, kind split): the forward-kinematics captures of the two URDF sources that BD-065 vendors, g1-urdf and iiwa7-urdf. Deps: BD-065, BD-067, STD-E2E. It is the only part of BD-067 that needs BD-065's vendored files and PROVENANCE.toml. It covers the [[model]] rows, capture_fk_urdf.py (fusestatic off, the 38-body check, mimic sampling), the URDF conventions block, five tests and its own script, oracle_urdf_fixtures.sh, which runs BD-067's hygiene script as a stage. Without the split, BD-067's MJCF fixtures and the hygiene gate waited on the URDF importer.

requests.what: Add dep N24bp4-01, and say that the URDF rows' oracle captures of g1-urdf and iiwa7-urdf come from N24bp4-01 (split from BD-067 this round), not from BD-067. BD-067 no longer depends on BD-065 and no longer captures the URDF files. Without the dep, N14b-24 can start its URDF rows before any capture exists, and they are logged 'not run' instead of measured.

The Out list (line 46) and line 122 name BD-067 for 'the captures of the two URDF sources'. They are now N24bp4-01's, which depends on this bead; name it there. Otherwise a reader looks in BD-067 for the URDF capture rows, which it no longer has.

Lines 127-128 say the fixture-capture bead 'follows this one in the bead graph (it needs an importer to name the bodies it captures)'. BD-067 no longer depends on BD-066: its scripts read the models and body names through the pinned oracle alone (audit note, applied). Restate the order of work: this bead closes on its hand-captured fixtures, and N14a-31 measures the full MJCF rows once BD-067's captures exist. As written, an implementer of BD-067 would wait for the importer, or build against it, against INV-GAUNT-01's rule that capture scripts read no workspace artifact.

eval.ledger's pending refusals: add sealed-object-exists (8xx, exit 7: a seal of a name already sealed in the campaign with different bytes; nothing is overwritten; observed the name and the stored digest), which BD-261 now raises. The row says only that such a seal 'writes nothing' and that the same bytes return the stored digest. Without a listed slug, an implementer has no code to return for different bytes and may overwrite the sealed answer key.

(1) Register the pending refusal sealed-object-exists (8xx, exit 7; BD-261's seal of an already-sealed name with other bytes). (2) The text for eval.ledger still cites FROB-REF-803 for a reused key on --open/--close, and qualification-undecided still spells --open. The actions are now --action open|close|seal of kind admin, with no key (--key is 802): a repeated open is campaign-already-open (exit 7, also for a battery label) and a repeated close is campaign-not-open (exit 3). Otherwise a reader of the registry tests for an 803 that the verb can never raise.

N24b-03 adds the declared-input check of sim.run --fixture (a declared --task is 802; an open --controller runs and is recorded), but the options it guards on the referee are yours at M1, and you depend on N24b-03. N24b-03's script can therefore test the check only in process. Add a sub-step to your script: frob sim run --fixture registry-demo --tier referee with --task <t> (expect 802) and with --controller <c> (runs; ControllerId in the run record), each under its own key. Otherwise no script ever exercises the check through the binary.

Your e2e section names N24b-20's steps variants_register and variants_run. N24b-20 (M1) no longer has them: an M1 script cannot depend on an M2 bead or skip its steps at run time (convention 7). Give the variants their own script, or a step in N24b-09's scripts/e2e/arena_fixture1_batch.sh if you depend on it. Otherwise the five variants have no end-to-end run.

Your capacity rule makes batch-cpu under the strict profile the adjudicator of the development set until FD-FSIM-13 lands. But the gate record's call 'frob task fixture quad-split-grip --layer batch --set development --reflect' names no tier or profile, and the manifest declares no axes.profile (N24bx-01). A batch-cpu run would therefore take the tier's default lockstep profile, and '--profile strict' would be 530. Declare axes.profile (strict, and referee if used) in the manifest. Then pass '--tier batch-cpu --profile strict' (or '--tier referee') on the development call and name that adjudicator in the gate row. N24b-13 does the same for the holdout. Otherwise the development set runs on a step that is not the registered adjudicator. Two more defects in your e2e section. (a) It has no script of its own (convention 11). It names N24b-22's steps check_task, settle, development_set and reflection, but N24b-22 depends on you (convention 7). Give BD-202 its own script built only on its deps, for example scripts/e2e/arena_fixture2_sets.sh, and N24b-22 will run it as a stage. (b) Its calls frob task fixture … --set development --tier referee --json (and --reflect) carry no --key, and compared runs need distinct keys (convention 5). They also hard-code --tier referee, against your own capacity rule.
